title: Hub registry: teams — spoke relationship groups with shared purpose and commercial intent
description: Extend hub registry with a teams concept. A team is a named group of spokes sharing a common interest, role, or commercial purpose. A spoke can belong to multiple teams with different relevance in each context. Teams are defined in the hub registry and used by Ozi/routing intelligence to determine: (1) whether cross-spoke suggestions are relevant, (2) how to frame messages (commercial vs internal vs standalone), (3) which spokes are never surfaced for publicizing wins. Example: 'wheelwright-team' = {framework, website, tracks} — commercially linked, wins worth publicizing. 'solutions-mv-hafinder' = {e-org, wheelwright} — different relevance, wheelwright appears in both but with different framing. A spoke with no team (e.g. a personal utility) is standalone — never suggested for cross-promotion.
perceive: Hub registry at {hub_path}/WAI-Hub/registry/ stores per-spoke entries (id, name, version, status, one_liner). No team concept exists. Ozi has no way to know whether two spokes are related, commercially linked, or completely independent. Routing intelligence (lug-routing-intelligence-20260330) depends on this to make proactive suggestions meaningful — without teams, Ozi cannot judge whether a framework win should trigger a website update suggestion.
execute: 1. Define teams schema: teams.json at {hub_path}/WAI-Hub/registry/teams.json. Structure: array of {id, name, purpose, commercial (bool), public_facing (bool), members: [{spoke_id, relevance_note}]}. 2. Extend spoke registry entry: add teams[] (list of team IDs this spoke belongs to). 3. Add standalone flag to spoke profile: standalone=true means never surface for cross-spoke suggestions. 4. Ozi routing logic: before surfacing a cross-spoke suggestion, check if source and target share a team. If no shared team → skip. If shared team → check commercial flag for framing. If target spoke is standalone → never suggest. 5. Document schema in hub registry reference. 6. Seed with initial teams for the wheelwright wheel.
verify: teams.json exists in hub registry with at least one team entry. Spoke entries reference team IDs. Ozi completing a framework lug (impact>=8) suggests website update only when framework and website share a team. Standalone spoke never appears in cross-spoke suggestions. Wheelwright appearing in two teams does not cause duplicate suggestions — team context determines framing.
acceptance_criteria: teams.json in hub registry: {id, name, purpose, commercial, public_facing, members[]}
Spoke registry entries include teams[] field
Standalone spoke flag prevents cross-spoke suggestions
Ozi checks shared team membership before surfacing cross-spoke suggestion
Commercial flag determines whether wins are framed for publicizing
Framework + website share a team — framework win triggers website suggestion
bygo-style isolated spoke never appears in cross-spoke suggestions
target_files: hub/tools/ozi_worker.py (cross-spoke suggestion check: shared team + commercial flag)
